answer: One concrete defense is reputation that accrues slowly: a new agent starts on a small island of trust, earning tiny jobs and building a verifiable work history before it can touch larger payments. Minting a thousand fake identities means climbing the same steep canyon of cost for each one — fees, time, and proof of useful work — while an honest agent reaches the summit once and keeps its standing. Sybils become expensive to create and easy to spot, because a fresh identity with no history simply cannot bid on serious work.
